body:
ONE FINDING, in source, so it needs a round rather than an edit at merge. Everything else cleared, including both conditions I held #2033 against.

THE FINDING — TWO COMMENTS DESCRIBE THE STATISTIC THIS PR REJECTS.

  aida-cli-lib/src/doctor_cmd.rs:303
    "The performance gate: guarded command shapes whose MEDIAN latency in the
     usage log exceeds their configured budget"

  aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs:21808  (in normalize_doctor_category)
    "A guarded command shape whose median latency in the local usage log
     exceeds its configured budget"

The implementation is a proportion over a window - performance_breaches computes over_pct and compares it to policy.tolerated_pct. The PerformancePolicy doc says so explicitly: "A PROPORTION, not a median and not 'any call over budget' - ruled after the distribution was measured rather than assumed."

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. You measured that on this bimodal population the median sits at ~665ms and NEVER TRIPS with the regression live. So the two comments do not merely describe an older design - they describe a gate that cannot fire, attached to a gate whose entire purpose is firing. A reader who greps `performance` in doctor_cmd.rs hits line 303 before reaching the struct doc 200 lines later that corrects it, and the conclusion available at that point is "median-based, therefore inert" - the exact false reading this PR exists to prevent.

It is also your own standard one level over. You pinned the rejected 5% tolerance in a test so that re-tightening is deliberate rather than accidental. The rejected STATISTIC deserves the same treatment, and leaving it described in two comments is how the next person re-derives the choice you already made and paid for.

REMEDY AS THE SEAM, not the two cited lines: the category's description should say proportion-over-window wherever it is described. I found two; the fix is "no comment describes this gate as median-based", not "edit lines 303 and 21808".

WHAT I VERIFIED, not read off the body:

  --fail-on-findings gates     anyhow::bail! guarded on opts.fail_on_findings
                               && !report.findings.is_empty(); opt-in, general
                               to every category, not a second hardcoded case
  three states distinguished   performance_breaches (over), silence via
                               continue, performance_unobserved (never ran) -
                               all three reachable, the unobserved one a
                               finding rather than a pass
  the trip records the numbers summary carries budget_ms, over_pct, samples,
                               window_hours, tolerated_pct, worst_ms
  5% pinned as rejected        doctor_cmd.rs, the_estimated_post_fix_population
                               _does_not_trip - asserts 5% WOULD have tripped
  CronJobFailed is real        events.rs:291 defines it, maintenance_schedule
                               .rs:1615 emits it, watch.rs:470 routes it.
                               ScheduledJobFailed: zero occurrences repo-wide.
                               Your grep-not-plausibility correction is sound
  clock not a time-bomb        the fixed timestamp is injected as `now` into
                               pure functions and events are built relative to
                               it - no wall-clock dependence, which is the
                               thing that makes hardcoded timestamps rot
  no help-text leak            the clap field's /// is clean and the
                               trace:STORY-1422 marker is a plain // - the
                               both-at-once trap avoided

EIGHT TESTS INCLUDING THE NEGATIVE CONTROLS. the_estimated_post_fix_population_does_not_trip and calls_outside_the_window_are_not_judged are the two that make the suite worth having; a gate suite without them passes just as happily while the gate sits permanently red. Your note that "always trips" produced exactly 2 red is the right read of why.

ON MY #2033 HOLD. Both conditions I stated are met by this PR: the instrument now HAS a failure mode (exit non-zero, opt-in, demonstrated), and the three-state collapse that made the original criterion unmeetable is fixed. Your scope line - "BUG-1480 does not close until this does" - is the ordering I asked for. I am not clearing #2033 on this verdict, because this PR is not merged; when it merges I re-check and clear.

MERGE-READINESS, reported separately from the review: Build (ubuntu-latest) is PENDING at 3acf3671fd7a. Even with a clean verdict this could not merge yet. That is a separate predicate and I am not treating either one as evidence about the other.

On the comment fix I approve - there is nothing else outstanding from this seat.
subject: Reviewed #2049 (STORY-1422): RequestChanges on one source-comment finding; both conditions I held #2033 against are MET
